events.description: S phase: DNA replication creates sister chromatids attached at centromeres; centrosome duplication begins.
constraints: Replication occurs during interphase, not during mitosis

events.description: G2: centrosome duplication completes; energy and proteins for chromosome manipulation are synthesized.
constraints: Final preparations must complete before mitosis entry

events.description: Prometaphase: nuclear envelope fragments; kinetochores bind spindle microtubules; sister kinetochores orient to opposite poles.
constraints: Kinetochores of sister chromatids must face opposite poles

events.description: Metaphase checkpoint: spindle checkpoint monitors attachment of all sister chromatids to microtubules from opposite poles before anaphase.
constraints: Anaphase separation is irreversible; cycle does not proceed until attachments are correct

events.description: Anaphase: spindle-driven motions separate duplicated chromosomes into two distinct sets moved toward opposite ends of the cell.
constraints: Requires controlled microtubule dynamics and motor enzyme activity

events.description: Telophase: chromosomes decondense, spindles break down, nuclear envelopes reform; nuclear division completes.
constraints: Events of early mitosis are reversed

events.description: Cytokinesis: physical separation of cytoplasmic components into two daughter cells; may be absent, yielding multinucleate cells.
constraints: Cytokinesis is distinct from nuclear division and can occur separately
